look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Find the rough triangular to broadly ovate leaf blades, usually unlobed or only shallowly lobed, on a long trailing vine. Look for small round, often striped young gourds. This is a perennial from a substantial tuberous rootstock; do not excavate plants merely to verify it. The staged photo shows the leaves, vines and striped fruits, not the underground root.
taxonomy_notes: POWO/FNA accept Cucurbita foetidissima Kunth; Cucurbita perennis is a synonym. Do not treat it as cultivated Cucurbita pepo, or infer three-county native PASS from Texas-level nativity.

morphology_keys.habit: Long-running, coarse, trailing perennial vine from a large perennial rootstock; stems rough and bearing tendrils.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Alternate, simple, rough leaves, typically triangular to broad-ovate, mostly unlobed or shallowly lobed; do not diagnose by odor alone.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: Separate male and female large yellow flowers on the same plant; inspect female inferior ovary below corolla and the calyx/corolla from the side.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Usually small globose gourds around 5–10 cm, green-striped when young and yellowing as mature; compare fruiting peduncle and seed with other Cucurbita.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Trailing rough stems with axillary tendrils; perennial rootstock is a distinguishing life-history character but not safely visible in a normal field photograph.

confused_with: Cucurbita pepo (annual crop or escape; usually more deeply 5–7-lobed leaves and strongly pustulate-based stem hairs; fruit shape varies widely)
Cucurbita melopepo (annual wild/cultivated concepts with often lobed leaves; cultivated pattypan shapes alone are not species proof)
comparisons.key_distinctions: Use a combination of broad mostly unlobed triangular rough leaves, small rounded gourds and perennial habit; smell and fruit stripes alone are not diagnostic.
